messages.subject: Nimble function issue
parts:
Hello Everyone,

I'm having some small issue with multiplying two scalars in my nimble model. I'm trying to write a code to generalize a time series model. So the psi[t] line in the gapCode is where i face the issue. I also tried using "inprod" function and matrix multplication "%*%" for durpar[1:p], g[(t-1):(t-p)] but it didn't work as these are scalars. I'm not sure how to solve this multiplication problem. Any help will be appreciated. 
Here is the reproducible code.

library(nimble)

gapCode <- nimbleCode({
  for (t in 1:mxpq){
    psi[t] <- omega
    g[t] ~ dgamma(shape=eta, scale=psi[t]/eta)
  }
  for( t in (mxpq+1):(T)){
    psi[t] <- omega+sum(durpar[1:p]*g[(t-1):(t-p)])+sum(durpar[(p+1):(p+q)]*psi[(t-1):(t-q)]) #this line is the issue
    g[t] ~ dgamma(shape=eta, scale=psi[t]/eta)
  }
  durpar[1:k] ~ ddirch(alpha=alpha[1:k])
  eta ~ dgamma(shape=0.001,scale=1/0.001)
  omega ~ dnorm(0,sd=100)
})

##########################
# Simulation:
##########################
set.seed(1)
p=2
q=1
mxpq <- max(p,q)
k=p+q+1
eta <- 2.2
omega <- 0.1
alpha <- c(0.25,0.05)
betastar <- c(0.6)
T <- 5000

psi_sim <- rep(NA,T)
g_sim <- rep(NA,T)

for (t in 1:mxpq){
  psi_sim[t] <- omega
  g_sim[t] <- rgamma(n=1, shape=eta, scale=psi_sim[t]/eta)
}
for (t in (mxpq+1):(T)){
  psi_sim[t] <- omega+alpha[1:p]%*%g_sim[(t-1):(t-p)]+betastar[1:q]%*%psi_sim[(t-1):(t-q)]
  g_sim[t] <- rgamma(n=1, shape=eta, scale=psi_sim[t]/eta)
}

# Running nimble code:
gapModel <- nimbleModel(code =  gapCode,
                             constants = list(T = T,p=p,q=q,k=k,mxpq=mxpq,alpha = rep(0.5, k))
                             ,data = list(g=g_sim)
                             ,inits = list(eta=1,omega=0.001))

mcmcConf <- configureMCMC(gapModel,monitors = c("eta","omega","durpar"),
                          useConjugacy = FALSE)
Rmcmc<-buildMCMC(mcmcConf)
Cmodel<-compileNimble(gapModel)
Cmcmc <- compileNimble(Rmcmc, project =  gapModel)
samplesList <- runMCMC(Cmcmc, niter = 10000, thin=1, nburnin = 1000
                       ,samplesAsCodaMCMC = TRUE)

Thanks in advance.

messages.author: f116cbe5c604c988
messages.subject: Re: Nimble function issue
parts:
Sreeram, thanks for your use of nimble, and there might be a few things going on here.

When you have q = 1, then:
p +1 = p + q

Thus, the indexing:
durpar[(p+1):(p+q)]
is really:
durpar[(p+1):(p+1)]
which doesn't work well with the compiler.

The same goes for
t - 1 = t - q
and the index:
psi[(t-1):(t-q)])
has a similar problem.  Specifically, this indexing doesn't work well with the sum() function.

If you want to use q = 1, then try changing the problematic line to:

psi[t] <- omega + sum(durpar[1:p]*g[(t-1):(t-p)]) + durpar[p+1]*psi[t-1]

Making that change, things seem to work ok for me.  But give it a try, and let us know.

Cheers,
Daniel

Any help with this will be appreciated.

parts:
Sreeram, can you try re-writing your method2, so that it *does not* include any *decreasing index ranges.  That is, you currently have:

g[(t-1):(t-p)]
which evaluates to g[ (t-1) : (t-2) ]
where the index range t-1 to t-2 is decreasing.

Can you try rearranging your vector variables, so that all the index ranges are *increasing*?  This might take a little bit of juggling indices, or declaration of new intermediate variables in the model, to reverse the indexing of the vectors (both) g[] and psi[].

I think this might be your problem here, but I'm sorry I can't try doing it right now. But please let me know if you're able to give this a try, and what you learn.

Cheers,
Daniel
